section.sectionSummaryBrief: Just as physical dew descends, so too the "dew of Torah" descends and is drawn into the Torah a person learns, with two aspects: the lower aspect drawn through human study and the higher aspect drawn from above, for which human study serves as a vessel, especially in the study of Pnimiyus HaTorah.
section.t: And behold, just as dew
(in its simple sense)
descends and is drawn downward,
so too is it with the dew of Torah,
which is drawn and revealed downward in the Torah that a person learns.
For in addition to the fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah
(the aspect of the dew of Torah)
is a granting of power to a person so that he can engage in Torah, and that through his engagement in Torah the Holy One, blessed be He, will read and review opposite him,
behold, also the matter of the dew of Torah itself is drawn and revealed downward in the Torah that a person learns.
For in the drawing down of the Torah above into the Torah that a person learns,
there are two matters.
The Torah as it is in the Z"T of Atik,
[is] the rain of Torah.
And the drawing down of this aspect is through a person's engagement in Torah,
for since the Z"T of Atik are invested in Arich, the root of the chain of descent,
therefore a person's engagement in Torah is an arousal from below that awakens and draws down this aspect.
And the Torah as it is in the G"R of Atik,
[is] the dew of Torah.
And the drawing down of this aspect is from above,
and a person's engagement in Torah is only like a vessel in which the dew of Torah is drawn and revealed.
And it can be said,
that this—that a person's study of Torah is a vessel for the dew of Torah—is primarily in the study of Pnimiyus HaTorah.
For since Pnimiyus HaTorah
(even as it is drawn downward)
is the Tree of Life, which is above the matter of clarifications,
therefore it is like a vessel for the essence of Torah, which is above any connection to the chain of descent
(the G"R of Atik, which are not invested in Arich),
the dew of Torah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on this, the two versions of the Sages' statement—"or Torah" and "tal Torah"—can be explained, where "or Torah" refers to Pnimiyus HaTorah, which serves as a vessel for "tal Torah."
section.t: And based on this, we can explain the connection between the two versions in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory,
"Whoever uses the light of Torah, the light of Torah revives him,"
for the version in the Gemara is "light of Torah" and the version in the Yalkut
is "dew of Torah,"
and it can be said,
that "light of Torah" is Pnimiyus HaTorah,
and the study of Pnimiyus HaTorah is a vessel for the dew of Torah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Similarly in prayer, although generally it is an elevation from below to above, it also contains the aspect of drawing down from above to below, beginning with the verse "Ad-nai, open my lips," which is prayed that one's speech be like Torah, drawing down God's own prayer.
section.t: And similarly is it in prayer,
for although in general it is an elevation from below to above,
it also contains the matter of drawing down from above to below.
And the explanation is,
that the beginning of the prayer of the Silent Amidah
[which is the main prayer]
is the verse,
"Ad-nai, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise,"
for the recitation of this verse is
(not only an introduction to prayer,
but rather)
the beginning of the prayer itself,
as it is stated in the Gemara
that it is like a long prayer.
And behold, in the Targum on the verse "Ad-nai, open my lips," it is translated,
"Open my lips in Torah."
That is,
that the request in this verse at the beginning of prayer is,
that the prayer
(and my mouth will declare Your praise)
should be like Torah
("Ad-nai, open my lips in Torah").
For just as in Torah,
the Torah that a person learns is the word of G-d,
"My words that I have placed in your mouth,"
and the person is like one who responds after the reader,
so too should the prayer be in the manner of "and my mouth will declare Your praise,"
that a person's prayer should be
(not his own prayer,
but rather)
that only through it will be drawn down
("declare" from the term "drawing down")
"Your praise,"
the prayer of the Holy One, blessed be He.
